name: Smart-wallet relay modules accept replayed owner and guardian signatures
summary: The wallet system's relayed execute() on its execution and recovery modules verifies the owner's or guardians' signature but never marks the signed message as used, and the recovery module's permissionless deadline setter can wrap a recovery deadline into the past. The attacker replayed a 2020 guardian signature to run and finalize a recovery that set wallet 0xe545's owner back to the signer of a 2021 swap signature, then replayed that swap 19 times to make the wallet buy MARK in a thin pool it had pumped, and did the same to wallet 0x5a79 with 9 replays; copycats replayed other wallets' old swap signatures the same way.
notes: Module implementations are unverified; the replay is visible in the anchor's trace, where byte-identical execute() calldata (nonce 1) to the execution module succeeds 19 times. The replayed signatures were first used in the 2020 and 2021 refs txs (per the DeFiHackLabs PoC).

The recovery module's reset (its 2021 upgrade) sets the age; the execution module last changed in September 2020. Wallets are proxies to 2020 implementations 0x66a3d4a9 and 0xf19d4c59 that only obey their modules, so they are victims, not targets.

Loss is the 20 drained wallets' ETH, USDC and UNI across the anchor and 26 copycat txs (loss.mjs, gross per rule 11), including gas refunds the replays paid to relayer 0xd33814c5. Tokens the replayed swaps bought for the wallets (MARK, KNC, BAL and others) are not subtracted (rule 11).
17 later txs from 0xde84434b through Multicall3 (blocks 26239624-26248898) replay recoveries without moving assets and are left out of the campaign.
